findings.claim: ADR 0043's amendment says 'the CLI holds nothing that changes a store' and ADR 0040's correction says the CLI 'no longer carries any verb that writes to a store'. Both are false: `kmaudit ui` writes feedback, verdicts and second opinions to the store, and with this change it reruns checks and saves their runs through POST /api/rerun.

The judge refusals for an unknown id still say 'list them with kmaudit claims list --claims' / 'kmaudit checks list'. With the CLI judge gone, only the judge MCP tool (and the page) reach these lines, and kmaudit's agents have no shell. They should name the claims_list / checks_list tools, the way every other MCP-facing message in this change does.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan asks.
`kmaudit --help` lists only mcp, ui, namespaces, briefing, claims list and checks list.
Each dropped verb is a hidden stub that takes any arguments, `--help` included, and exits 2 with one stderr line naming its MCP tool.
guard.py is gone.
POST /api/rerun calls `check_verbs.run` on the server's root, which is the same namespace the page's /api/data builds from.
It sits behind the same Host, Origin, Content-Type and Content-Length checks as the other writes.
No string in kmaudit's source or ui.html names a dropped verb as a command, and no doc, skill, agent or kmctl file outside history does either.
Two non-blocking doc fixes remain.
Gates: `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format, tests, integration and eval rows r1 to r4 all pass; "stamp green: 9eac5b5209ea2a3b3e053523f85701b4cf46dd2530a7c914d9a641decf5a9902".

Read cli.py, ui.py, ui.html, mcp_server.py, check_verbs.py and judge.py in full where they changed, plus the diffs of verbs.py, sections.py, coverage.py, briefing.py, instructions.py, check_instructions.py, models.py, README, commands.md, manifesto, overview, ADR 0040 and ADR 0043.
r1: test_cli_slim.py checks the visible command set at the click level and in `--help`, and runs each of the nine dropped verbs bare, with arguments and with `--help`.
It asserts exit 2, empty stdout, one stderr line and the tool's name.
A verb that still ran, or a missing kept command, fails it.
r2: test_audit_ui.py makes the `exits` check stale, then POSTs /api/rerun.
It asserts `rerun == 1`, the claim's row reran, and /api/data then shows it not stale and holding.
It also checks the endpoint calls `check_verbs.run`, that a cross-site Origin gets 403 and leaves the check stale, and that the page has the button.
The endpoint stays safe: a cross-site browser POST needs a preflight for application/json, which the server never answers, and any Origin it does send must match the Host.

r3: the source scan works line by line, so I also joined wrapped lines and re-scanned all of kmaudit's .py files and ui.html for `kmaudit claims|checks|judge|coverage|guard` and bare `claims todo` / `checks run` forms.
It found nothing.
A repo-wide git grep outside .loop found only history: older ADRs, prototypes and skill eval results.md logs.
The ADR 0043 test anchors to the amendment's text.
r4: compared the test names before and after.
The only CLI-only tests deleted are the ones the briefing lists: submit from a file, the people-facing todo counts, the coverage text summary, test_audit_guard.py and the `checks run` exit code.
That last one became a check of the function's `fails` status.
The judge, namespaces, briefing and independent tests now drive `run_judge`, `verbs` and `check_verbs` directly, with the same assertions on content.
They no longer assert exit codes.
The MCP refusal prefix change is matched in test_mcp.py.
No skill, agent or doc matched the old `kmaudit VERB: refused:` prefix.

f1: ADR 0043's line "the CLI holds nothing that changes a store" and ADR 0040's correction "no longer carries any verb that writes to a store" overstate it, because `kmaudit ui` writes to the store and now reruns checks.
Say instead that no command writes except through the page.
f2: judge.py:234 and :244 send an MCP caller to shell commands.
Name the claims_list and checks_list tools there, or both.
After one rerun, `lastRun` in ui.html stays on the bar through later Reloads.
That is harmless, but it can show a stale "Reran 1 check." Two reruns at once from two tabs both run every stale check.
The store's write lock or the sqlite error path covers that.
